facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically from the Aptian to Albian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian),

facts.statement: The genus Tenontosaurus was described by John Ostrom in 1970.
facts.quote: authority: Ostrom, 1970

facts.statement: The genus contains two species: the type species T. tilletti described by Ostrom in 1970 and T. dossi described by Winkler, Murry, and Jacobs in 1997.
facts.quote: subdivision: †T. tilletti Ostrom, 1970 (type) †T. dossi Winkler, Murry & Jacobs, 1997

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus is classified as an iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus ( ; ) is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus possessed an unusually long and broad tail that was stiffened by a network of bony tendons, similar to its back.
facts.quote: It had an unusually long, broad tail, which like its back was stiffened with a network of bony tendons.

facts.statement: The first Tenontosaurus fossil was discovered in Big Horn County, Montana, by an AMNH expedition in 1903.
facts.quote: The first Tenontosaurus fossil was found in Big Horn County, Montana by an American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) expedition in 1903.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown informally named the animal "Tenantosaurus" or "sinew lizard" due to its stiffening tendons.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown gave it the informal name "Tenantosaurus", "sinew lizard", in reference to the extensive system of stiffening tendons in its back and tail.

facts.statement: John Ostrom scientifically described the taxon as Tenontosaurus tilletti in 1970 based on fossils from the Cloverly Formation.
facts.quote: Following his expedition, in 1970, Ostrom published a review of the fauna and geology of the Cloverly Formation. In that paper, he scientifically described Brown's taxon, calling it Tenontosaurus tilletti.

facts.statement: The species name 'tilletti' honors the Lloyd Tillett family, who assisted Yale field parties.
facts.quote: The species name refers to the Lloyd Tillett family, who provided field parties from Yale with assistance and hospitality throughout their expeditions.

facts.statement: A new species, T. dossi, was described in 1997 from remains found at the Doss Ranch site in Texas.
facts.quote: In 1997, remains from the Twin Mountains Formation of Texas were assigned to a new species of Tenontosaurus, T. dossi, named after the Doss Ranch site.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus fossils were unearthed from the Yucca Formation in Texas in 2025.
facts.quote: In 2025, Tenontosaurus were unearthed from the Yucca Formation in Texas.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated that T. dossi was 7 meters long and weighed 1000 kg.
facts.quote: Paul also estimated that T. dossi would have been 7 m long and weighed 1000 kg.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was a facultative quadruped capable of standing on either two or four legs.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was a facultative quadruped, capable of assuming either a bipedal or quadrupedal stance.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus likely used a quadrupedal stance for feeding but was probably unable to move rapidly on four legs.
facts.quote: It may have used a quadrupedal stance while feeding, but was probably incapable of rapid quadrupedal movement.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had a thick, U-shaped beak formed by flaring premaxillae, a trait characteristic of iguanodontians.
facts.quote: The premaxillae flared inferiorly (towards the bottom), forming a thick, U-shaped beak, characteristic of iguanodontians.

facts.statement: The vomer was the longest bone in the Tenontosaurus skull, extending from the beak to the back of the eye socket.
facts.quote: The single longest bone in Tenontosaurus' skull is the vomer, which stretches from the middle of the beak to the very back of the orbital cavity (eye socket).

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Tenontosaurus ended in a predentary bone, a structure unique to ornithischians that formed the lower beak.
facts.quote: It terminated in a predentary bone, a structure found uniquely among ornithischians which formed the lower beak.

facts.statement: All teeth of Tenontosaurus were enameled on only one side, the medial or inner surface.
facts.quote: All of Tenontosaurus' teeth were enameled unilaterally (on only one side, that being medially, or on the inside).

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ostrom's original reconstruction of the Tenontosaurus skull accurately represented its true depth, as it may have been exaggerated.
facts.quote: Ostrom's reconstruction of the skull exaggerated the overall depth of the skull, leading to one which more closely resembles that of Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was originally placed in the family Iguanodontidae but later reclassified into Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was originally classified in the family Iguanodontidae, although subsequent authors challenged this classification and proposed it actually belonged to Hypsilophodontidae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies describe Tenontosaurus as an intermediate non-dryomorph iguanodont between Hypsilophodon-like and Iguanodon-like taxa.
facts.quote: Subsequent phylogenetic analyses have found Tenontosaurus to be intermediate in position between Hypsilophodon-like taxa and Iguanodon-like taxa, as a non-dryomorph iguanodont.

facts.statement: Scientists debate Tenontosaurus's exact phylogenetic position, with some studies linking it closer to dryomorphs and others placing it as a sister taxon to a clade of rhabdodontids and dryomorphs.
facts.quote: The precise phylogenetic position of Tenontosaurus varies between studies, with some studies finding it to be more closely related to dryomorphs than rhabdodontids, some studies finding it to be the sister taxon of a clade uniting rhabdodontids and dryomorphs.

facts.statement: A 2024 study proposed that Tenontosaurus belongs to the new family Tenontosauridae within the Rhabdodontomorpha.
facts.quote: A similar result was recovered by Fonseca et al. (2024), who found Iani, Tenontosaurus, and also Convolosaurus to form the new family Tenontosauridae within the Rhabdodontomorpha

facts.statement: Adult Tenontosaurus could browse vegetation up to a height of about 3 meters when standing on two legs.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was a low browser, and an adult would have had a maximum browsing height of about 3 m if it adopted a bipedal stance.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had a powerful U-shaped beak and angled teeth that allowed it to consume leaves, wood, and fruit.
facts.quote: Its powerful, U-shaped beak and the angled cutting surfaces of its teeth, however, meant it was not limited to which part of the plant it consumed.

facts.statement: Fossils of the carnivorous theropod Deinonychus are frequently found associated with Tenontosaurus tilletti remains.
facts.quote: Teeth and a number of skeletons belonging to the carnivorous theropod Deinonychus have often been discovered associated with Tenontosaurus tilletti remains.

facts.statement: Approximately 20% of Tenontosaurus fossils are found near Deinonychus, leading some scientists to suggest Deinonychus was its major predator.
facts.quote: In all, 20% of Tenontosaurus fossils are found in close proximity to Deinonychus, and several scientists have suggested that this implies Deinonychus was the major predator of Tenontosaurus.

facts.statement: Deinonychus likely preyed on juvenile Tenontosaurus, as adults were too large to be effective targets.
facts.quote: It is likely that Deinonychus favored juvenile Tenontosaurus, and that when Tenontosaurus reached a certain size, it passed out of range as a food source for the small theropods

facts.statement: Medullary bone tissue found in a Tenontosaurus specimen indicates it used this tissue for reproduction, a trait also found in birds.
facts.quote: The presence of medullary bone tissue in the thigh bone and shin bone of one specimen indicates that Tenontosaurus used this tissue, today only found in birds that are laying eggs, in reproduction.

facts.statement: A Tenontosaurus individual died at the age of 8 years before reaching full adult size.
facts.quote: the tenontosaur individual was not at full adult size upon her death at 8 years old.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus grew rapidly in early life and during sub-adulthood but slowed significantly near maturity, unlike other iguanodontians.
facts.quote: A histological study showed that T. tilletti grew quickly early in life and during sub-adult ontogeny, but grew very slowly in the years approaching maturity, unlike other iguanodontians.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived in a paleoenvironment of tropical or sub-tropical forests, floodplains, and swamps similar to modern-day Louisiana.
facts.quote: The paleoenvironment of the Antlers Formation consisted of tropical or sub-tropical forests, floodplains, river deltas, coastal swamps, bayous and lagoons, probably similar to that of modern-day Louisiana.

facts.statement: In the arid Little Sheep Mudstone Member, Tenontosaurus was the only herbivorous dinosaur present.
facts.quote: In the arid Little Sheep Mudstone Member, Tenontosaurus is the only herbivorous dinosaur

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was the most abundant vertebrate in the Cloverly Formation, five times more common than the next most frequent species.
facts.quote: Throughout the Cloverly Formation, Tenontosaurus is by far the most common vertebrate, five times more abundant than the next most common, the ankylosaur Sauropelta.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, between approximately 122 and 108 million years ago, from the Aptian to the Albian stages.
facts.quote: que vivieron a mediados del período Cretácico, entre aproximadamente 122 a 108 millones de años desde el Aptiense al Albiense

facts.statement: The time range for Tenontosaurus is recorded as the Aptian to Cenomanian, spanning from 121.4 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (121.4 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: When Tenontosaurus first appeared in Wyoming and Montana during the early Albian age, the climate was arid to semi-arid with seasonal rainfall and occasional droughts.
facts.quote: At the time Tenontosaurus first appeared in Wyoming and Montana (the early Albian age), the regions climate was arid to semi-arid, dry, with seasonal periods of rainfall and occasional droughts.

facts.statement: An apparent increase in the abundance of Tenontosaurus coincided with a dramatic shift in the regional climate.
facts.quote: This dramatic shift in climate coincided with an apparent increase, rather than decrease, in the abundance of Tenontosaurus.

facts.statement: The species Tenontosaurus tilletti was described by John Ostrom in 1970.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus tilletti, descrito por John Ostrom en 1970

facts.statement: The species Tenontosaurus dossi was described by Winkler, Murray, and Jacobs in 1997.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus dossi,descrito por Winkler, Murry y Jacobs en 1997

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus dossi is known only from a handful of specimens collected from the Twin Mountains Formation in Parker County, Texas, USA.
facts.quote: T. dossi se conoce sólo por un puñado de especímenes recolectados en la Formación Twin Mountains del condado de Parker, Texas, Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus measured between 6.5 and 8 meters in length, 2.2 meters in height, and weighed between 1 and 2 tons.
facts.quote: Los tenontosaurios median entre 6,5 y 8 metros de longitud, 2,2 de altura y pesaba de 1 a 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of T. tilletti at 6 meters and the weight at 600 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul le dio a T. tillettorum una longitud más corta de 6 metros con un peso de 600 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus dossi would have been slightly larger, measuring seven meters in length and weighing one ton.
facts.quote: T. dossi habría sido un poco más grande con siete metros y una tonelada.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul provided values for Tenontosaurus of 6 to 7 meters in length and 600 to 1000 kilograms in weight.
facts.quote: En 2016 dio valores de 6 a7 metros de largo y entre 600 a 1000 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had long forelimbs with five stout fingers, a medium-sized curved skull, a robust body, and a very long tail that was twice the length of the torso; its back and tail were rigid due to a network of bony tendons, likely obliging it to walk on four legs for long periods, while its head ended in a beak with teeth aligned on the sides and its long hind legs had four stout toes.
facts.quote: Presentaban extremidades delanteras largas con manos provistas de cinco rollizos dedos, cráneo curvo y mediano, cuerpo robusto y corpulento, cola larga lo era más que los otros miembros de su familia y era el doble del largo del torso, que al igual que su espalda estaba rígida con una red de tendones óseos, cosa que lo habría obligado a andar mucho tiempo en cuatro patas, Su cabeza terminaba en pico con muelas alineadas a los lados y sus piernas eran largas con patas provistas de cuatro rollizos dedos.

facts.statement: The skull of Tenontosaurus is low and long, very elongated when viewed from above, with a conspicuous rounded widening at the snout tip and very wide lower sides at the rear.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Tenontosaurus es bajo y largo, muy alargado cuando se ve desde arriba, con la punta del hocico mostrando un ensanchamiento redondeado conspicuo y los lados inferiores de la parte posterior muy anchos.

facts.statement: When viewed from above, the lower jaw of Tenontosaurus has a U-shape.
facts.quote: En la vista superior, esta mandíbula tiene forma de U.

facts.statement: The true dentary teeth of the lower jaw have a prominent vertical main crest.
facts.quote: Los dientes dentarios verdaderos de la mandíbula inferior tienen una cresta principal vertical prominente.
